candidates: When constraining atoms by species, prefer `FixAtoms(mask=atoms.symbols == 'Element')` over manually computed boolean or integer index masks — this is the modern, idiomatic ASE pattern and reads closer to the physical intent.

Do not manually override or print `pbc` on structures returned by ASE surface builders (e.g. `fcc110`, `fcc111`, `bcc110`): the builders already configure the physically correct xy-periodic boundary conditions for slabs. Adding z-periodicity to a slab model is a physical error.
Use `atoms.symbols.search('Element')` to retrieve atom indices for a given chemical species rather than writing multi-line manual searches or index comprehensions over atom symbols.

Tutorial and example code that involves stochastic or random behaviour must create a local seeded generator with `np.random.default_rng(seed)` and pass it explicitly to each algorithm. Do not seed the global numpy RNG (`np.random.seed`) in documentation examples, as that pollutes the global state and is considered bad practice in scientific Python.

Any ASE class or function that performs random number generation internally should expose an `rng` keyword argument (defaulting to `np.random` for backwards compatibility) so callers can supply a `numpy.Generator` instance for reproducibility. Follow `ase.md.velocitydistribution` as the canonical project example of this pattern.
